title: Integrity Authentication in Tree Models

problem.claim: The paper studies authenticating whether deployed tree models have been tampered with or compromised.

contributions.claim: An authentication framework embeds a signature in a tree model and authenticates its existence using a small number of black-box queries.
The method locates selected leaves and modifies their prediction values without requiring training data, testing data, or retraining.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that this is the first study of signature embedding on tree models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on many public classification datasets reportedly show a high success rate with minimal accuracy loss.

narrative_sequence.summary: Tree models are widely used in machine learning and data mining.
The work addresses model integrity authentication for detecting tampering or compromise in deployed tree models.
The framework embeds signatures by modifying selected leaf prediction values and verifies them with a small number of black-box queries, without training, testing data, or retraining.
The authors report experiments across many public classification datasets with high success and minimal accuracy loss.

unknowns: The abstract does not give the exact number of black-box queries.
The abstract does not quantify success rates or accuracy loss.
The threat model, attack resistance, baselines, and experimental protocol are unspecified.
